description_full: ScanSource, Inc. engages in the distribution of technology products and solutions in the United States, Brazil, and internationally. It operates through two segments: Specialty Technology Solutions, and Intelisys & Advisory. The Specialty Technology Solutions segment offers mobility and barcode, including mobile computing; barcode scanners and imagers, radio frequency identification devices, barcode printing and related services; point of sale systems and integrated pos software platforms; payment terminals, such as self-service kiosks, payment terminals and mobile payment devices; physical security comprising video surveillance and analytics, and video management software and access control; networking, such as switching, and routing and wireless products and software; communications, including voice, video, communication platform integration, and contact center solutions; managed connectivity and wireless enablement solutions. This segment offers applications that have evolved from traditional uses, such as inventory control, materials handling, distribution, shipping and warehouse management, and healthcare applications. The Intelisys & Advisory segment offers connectivity and software-defined networking, CX (unified communications as a service and contact center as a service), cloud/data center, security, managed AI, and wireless and IOT. This segment helps channel sales partners service various end users, including businesses of all sizes. It serves manufacturing, warehouse and distribution, retail and e-commerce, hospitality, transportation and logistics, government, education and healthcare, and other industries. ScanSource, Inc. was incorporated in 1992 and is headquartered in Greenville, South Carolina.

financial_summary: ScanSource, Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $886M market cap on $3.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -5% over the past three years and -1% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 8% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 11% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $114M in free cash flow — roughly 4 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.56× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.1× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 15× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 11.1% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 2.5% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 3% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.13x its revenue share).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-8.1% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 535 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 60% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 17% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 35% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 43% and a beta of 1.08, it moves roughly with the market.
About $15.6M trades a day, enough to build a position, and interest is running hot at 1.6x its yearly average volume.
In past sell-offs it fell 60% in the 2020 crash, 36% in the 2022 bear market and 62% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 37% below its DCF fair value of $69.04, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 33%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $55.00 to $88.96 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 13.7 vs 24.4, EV/EBITDA 10.4 vs 16.1 and P/FCF 7.8 vs 23.3 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 14% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 12.9% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 7.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 2 covering analysts target $64.50 on average, 48% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 8% falls short of the cost of capital of 10.0%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.61).
It runs a 11% gross margin and converts 4% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.56x.
ROE of 9% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.1x equity multiplier).
It spends 0.4% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.1x net debt to EBITDA ($88.4M of cash against $101.4M of debt), with interest covered 15.0x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.5, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at -5.2% over 3 years, 0.5% over 5 years and -0.9% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded -0.1% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex runs only 0.4x depreciation (0.3% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 4, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.5%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (12 sales, net $6.1M sold).
It returns 11.1% a year to shareholders (11.1% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 4.5% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 2,100 employees, each generates about $1.5M of revenue, 4.0x the Technology median.
That works out to $54K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $3.6M (2x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
